briefs.title: Markets Turn on the AI Buildout, Iran Talks Stall on Sequencing, Two Senate Seats Still Open
briefs.bluf: The Iran war is still the defining factor. Three more tankers were damaged near Qatar on November 5, Trump said he may have to destroy the rest of the country, and a carrier group is heading to the region, while Qatar shuttles a plan that trades lifting the blockade and IAEA access for reopening Hormuz. Wall Street had its worst day in years: the Nasdaq fell 5.5% and the Nasdaq 100 6.4%, its worst session since March 2020, on fears that a Democratic Congress slows the AI buildout; futures point to a partial rebound this morning. Democrats hold 54 Senate seats with Mississippi (a margin of about 138 votes) and Alaska (ranked choice tally November 18) still open, and a Justice Department suit over a second Dan Sullivan on the Alaska ballot is the main certification risk. In Cuba, Yoani Sánchez was released after more than nine hours, but two other independent journalists remain jailed and the Law 186 government overhaul takes effect November 9. Ukraine talks move to Abu Dhabi November 10 to 11 after a White House event marking the Oleshky humanitarian truce.
briefs._s: markets turn on the ai buildout, iran talks stall on sequencing, two senate seats still open the iran war is still the defining factor. three more tankers were damaged near qatar on november 5, trump said he may have to destroy the rest of the country, and a carrier group is heading to the region, while qatar shuttles a plan that trades lifting the blockade and iaea access for reopening hormuz. wall street had its worst day in years: the nasdaq fell 5.5% and the nasdaq 100 6.4%, its worst session since march 2020, on fears that a democratic congress slows the ai buildout; futures point to a partial rebound this morning. democrats hold 54 senate seats with mississippi (a margin of about 138 votes) and alaska (ranked choice tally november 18) still open, and a justice department suit over a second dan sullivan on the alaska ballot is the main certification risk. in cuba, yoani sánchez was released after more than nine hours, but two other independent journalists remain jailed and the law 186 government overhaul takes effect november 9. ukraine talks move to abu dhabi november 10 to 11 after a white house event marking the oleshky humanitarian truce. two senate races still open democrats hold 54 seats and flipped iowa, kansas, maine, ohio, north carolina, south carolina and texas. in mississippi, democrat scott colom leads sen. cindy hyde-smith 49.0% to 48.9% with about 3,600 mail ballots left; certification is due november 13. in alaska, mary peltola leads sen. dan sullivan 48.2% to 47.9% with ranked choice results due november 18. doj suit could stall alaska certification the justice department sued in october to block certification if peltola wins by less than the vote total of a second, unaffiliated candidate named daniel j. sullivan, arguing voters may have been confused. trump said he ordered the suit and has urged prosecuting peltola. legal scholars say the statute does not let doj enjoin a state certification. judge pauses the trump arch; la picks a new mayor a federal judge blocked construction of the planned arch for 14 days. in los angeles, nithya raman defeated mayor karen bass. in california, gov. newsom commuted 548 death sentences. more tankers hit; trump weighs a heavier strike the irgc said three more tankers were damaged november 5, two by mines and one by fire. ukmto reported a tanker hit by two projectiles 50 nautical miles north of madinat ash shamal, qatar. trump said he would rather not destroy the rest of the country but may have to, met his national security team, and spoke with the qatari emir, who urged restraint. a carrier group is heading to the region via singapore. diplomacy stuck on sequencing iran sent a nuclear proposal through qatar that it will discuss only after the us meets seven demands, including lifting sanctions and paying war reparations. a qatari draft reported by axios has the us lift the blockade and release some frozen funds and iran invite the iaea to bombed sites on day one, with hormuz reopening on day two and nuclear talks on the enriched uranium stockpile after that. iranian sources told reuters another us attack is more likely than a deal. tehran leans on the region foreign minister araghchi called his counterparts in the uae, qatar, saudi arabia, turkey, pakistan, oman and egypt. parliament speaker qalibaf mocked vice president vance as a losing gambler after vance blamed the war for the midterm losses. israel: herzog weighs who forms the next government after the october 27 election left netanyahu's bloc at 53 seats and gadi eisenkot's at 48, president herzog began consultations, meeting the smallest parties first. eisenkot was expected to have more endorsements than netanyahu. the election commission reviewed 9,069 polling stations and found no fraud. white house marks the oleshky truce melania trump hosted russian envoy kirill dmitriev and ukraine's david arakhamia to mark the six day humanitarian ceasefire in occupied oleshky (october 27 to november 1). more than 750 people were evacuated; russia refused to extend it. president trump met dmitriev but not the ukrainians and predicted a deal soon. abu dhabi talks next week witkoff and kushner lead the us side at three way talks in abu dhabi november 10 to 11. german chancellor merz hosts a coalition of the willing summit november 19. russia holds about 80% of donetsk. yoani sánchez released; two journalists still held yoani sánchez, director of 14ymedio, was released after more than nine hours in custody. adelth bonne gamboa of cubanet, arrested november 2, and henry constantín, jailed since september 16, remain detained. rsf, the inter american press association and amnesty international condemned the detentions. law 186 reshapes the government from november 9 the law, approved july 30 and published november 2 in the gaceta oficial, cuts the cabinet to 20 ministries plus the central bank and merges commerce, construction and agriculture into fewer bodies. officials present it as streamlining; critics see a shuffle that leaves the economic model untouched. protest count stays high the observatorio cubano de conflictos logged 542 protests and complaints in october and 85 repressive events. transition quiet no new annulment filings or street mobilization found. lula takes office january 1. pope leo begins south america tour the first us born pope is in uruguay november 6 to 8, argentina november 8 to 11 and peru november 11 to 17, about 50 events in 10 cities, including a return to chiclayo, where he was bishop, and a meeting with president milei. former fbi agent charged doj charged former fbi agent andrew reyes on november 5. details of the charges were not collected this cycle. election claims fade, alaska suit gives them a new hook rigging claims about the midterms have lost momentum as most losers conceded, but the doj suit over the second dan sullivan gives the "stolen seat" framing a new focus in alaska. fridge hacks: still no attribution no group has claimed or been named for the attacks on supermarket refrigeration controllers. belgium opened a prosecution and the eu called them deliberate. the danfoss and copeland flaws were disclosed by claroty august 9; forescout counted about 13,000 exposed systems. the pentagon is reviewing august freezer failures at military commissaries. mexican judge arrested in ryan wedding case a mexican judge was arrested over an alleged $2 million bribe tied to the case against ryan wedding, the former olympic snowboarder accused of running a cocaine network and ordering the killing of a federal witness. wedding was captured in mexico in january. doj launches super intelligence task force the department announced a task force on ai related crime the same day it charged a $129 million fraud marketed as a super intelligence investment. no new ofac actions found for november context: the cartel del noreste was designated october 13, venezuela's jorge rodríguez was delisted october 14, and foreign banks must exit panama's bicsa by november 14. deportations deepen school enrollment drops npr reports ice enforcement is accelerating enrollment declines in districts with large immigrant populations. doj also sued penn state over in state tuition for undocumented students. why the doomsday date keeps spreading writers revisiting the 1960 "doomsday" paper note that a specific date, a real scientific source and a friday the 13th make a claim shareable. the historian alan maceachern argues the lesson is about how confidently findings are presented. ai selloff after the election nvidia fell 9.2%, about $440 billion in value, and the largest tech stocks lost more than $1 trillion as investors priced in a congress that may slow data center and chip spending. south korea's kospi fell about 8 to 9% and halted trading. google: accept ai or lose search in schools from early 2027, gemini and search will be off by default on k-12 student accounts; schools that switch ai off entirely will also lose search. fairplay urged schools to consider other search engines. supreme court hears labor visa case november 10 department of labor v. sun valley orchards is argued monday. claim: a scientist said the world ends november 13 the date comes from a real 1960 science paper. its authors fitted a curve to population history that reached infinity in late 2026, and they picked friday the 13th partly as a joke. population growth peaked soon after and the curve stopped matching reality. hundreds leave oleshky more than 750 civilians left the occupied town during the six day truce, the largest humanitarian pause of the war in that area. the midterms were rigged through fake ballots and compromised machines democrats won by importing foreigners and registering them to vote (great replacement framing) ebola is a hoax, a western bioweapon, or a scheme for aid groups to make money a scientist predicted the world ends on friday, november 13, 2026 russian deepfake campaign against democrats (matryoshka / operation overload and storm-1516) inauthentic accounts in competitive races, hitting both parties far right networks break with trump after the losses

briefs.title: Baseline Edition: A Gulf War Under Domestic Pressure, a Hybrid Campaign in Europe, and Cuba Under Strain
briefs.bluf: The defining factor this week is the collision between the US war on Iran and US domestic politics: Democrats won both chambers on November 3 and the Vice President publicly blamed the war. Washington struck Iranian targets near Hormuz on the eve of the vote and tankers keep burning near the strait, while talks run through Gulf mediators. In Europe, a wave of hoax bomb threats against flights fits the pattern of a Russian linked hybrid campaign, unattributed so far. Russia killed 42 people at a Ukrainian aid center days before US mediated talks on November 10 and 11. Cuba is under severe strain from the oil blockade and is detaining independent journalists. This is the baseline edition, so status changes are measured from here.
briefs._s: baseline edition: a gulf war under domestic pressure, a hybrid campaign in europe, and cuba under strain the defining factor this week is the collision between the us war on iran and us domestic politics: democrats won both chambers on november 3 and the vice president publicly blamed the war. washington struck iranian targets near hormuz on the eve of the vote and tankers keep burning near the strait, while talks run through gulf mediators. in europe, a wave of hoax bomb threats against flights fits the pattern of a russian linked hybrid campaign, unattributed so far. russia killed 42 people at a ukrainian aid center days before us mediated talks on november 10 and 11. cuba is under severe strain from the oil blockade and is detaining independent journalists. this is the baseline edition, so status changes are measured from here. democrats win the house and senate democrats are projected to exceed 250 house seats and hold at least 54 senate seats. alaska (peltola leads sullivan by 637 votes) and mississippi (colom leads hyde smith by about 1,100) remain too close to call. vance blames the iran war for the losses the vice president wrote that the war was the reason republicans lost. trump acknowledged gas prices hurt but said he would go to war again. house leadership reshuffle speaker johnson will not seek to lead house republicans. scalise and jordan are running for minority leader; jeffries is running for speaker when congress convenes january 3. us strikes near hormuz on the eve of the midterms limited us strikes hit around qeshm, hengam and bandar abbas. iran's supreme national security council head said the strait stays closed until us addresses its conditions: lifting the naval blockade, waiving oil sanctions and a ceasefire including lebanon. more tankers on fire east of hormuz; tanker hit off qatar iranian state media reported two more tankers on fire. separately, the british military said a tanker was struck by projectiles off qatar. iran's security chief meets putin mohsen rezaei discussed regional issues in moscow, and iran says it will supply russian gas to neighboring countries. gaza and yemen at least four palestinians were killed in gaza on november 5. in yemen's taiz, government forces say they repelled a houthi attack; the un says water production has halved and hospitals are short of fuel. aid center strike toll reaches 42 russian bunker busting bombs hit a school used as an aid hub in komyshuvakha, then the shelter where people took cover. erdogan wants direct talks with putin; italy readies aid after talks with zelenskyy, erdogan said he wants to discuss ending the war with putin. italy is finalizing a new military aid package. putin seizes japan tobacco's russian operations; drone strike hits ozon warehouse moscow took control of jti's russian business. a drone strike set an ozon warehouse ablaze in southern russia. pla activity rebounds after typhoon lull 85 sorties from october 26 to november 1, 47 into the adiz. on november 3 to 4: 22 sorties, 7 pla navy ships and 5 official ships. beijing's ai enabled influence operations ahead of taiwan's local elections taiwanese officials report ai generated content and cyberattacks aimed at polarization and lower turnout before the november 28 vote. vietnam comments on china and laos military cooperation hanoi said the cooperation should contribute to regional stability. yoani sánchez detained in havana the 14ymedio founder was held about nine hours, the third detention of an independent journalist in havana this week after cubanet's camila acosta on tuesday. the us condemned the arrests. grid at about a third of demand the une forecast 958 mw available against 2,850 mw demand on november 2, with blackouts over 20 hours a day. government reorganization takes effect november 9 law 186 cuts central state agencies from 27 to 21. reported military mobilization cibercuba reports cuba mobilizing forces amid rising tensions with the us. transition settling after contested runoff lula won 51.8% to 48.2%. flávio bolsonaro's party acknowledged the result after his annulment call; trump called it rigged. colombia ends 'total peace' congress passed president de la espriella's bill: armed group members must disarm, identify fellow members, hand over recruited minors, surrender assets and reveal links to politicians to earn reduced sentences. leaders face at least 10 years. paraguay seizes bank tied to the president central bank took over ueno bank after its capital fell below half the legal minimum; about 3 million accounts and public pension funds frozen. poland arrests four over military supplies sent to russia part of a broader pattern of sabotage and procurement networks targeting the main aid route to ukraine. hoax bomb threats hit european aviation about ten flights threatened november 3 and four prague bound planes november 5. the eu transport chief says it is too early to say whether they are linked. prc influence operations target taiwan's november 28 vote officials cite ai generated content designed to polarize and depress turnout. narrative watch: iranian leadership messaging a statement attributed to mojtaba khamenei claims iran's control of hormuz shattered the myth of american invincibility. supermarket refrigeration systems hacked across europe unidentified hackers shut down supermarket fridges in several countries the same week as the flight threats; analysts see a pattern of low cost disruption. october ransomware roundup october incidents included a ransomware attack that disrupted patient care and surgeries at university of new mexico health sciences center. israel detains journalist abed abu shehadeh police and shin bet arrested the arab48 editor and +972 contributor in jaffa; a court extended his detention. rights groups call it part of a campaign against palestinian journalists. paraguay: ueno bank arrests prosecutors ordered the arrest of eight people including the bank's president and ceo. brazil: banco master case flávio bolsonaro is under investigation in the banco master case without formal charges, per mercopress. bangladesh garment workers win wage concessions after five days of protests and clashes with police, a new wage board agreed to a revised pay scale from december. workers seek about $242 a month. greek students march for education funding students marched in athens demanding affordable housing and more state investment in education. judge blocks deportations of afghans to afghanistan or pakistan a federal judge in new york temporarily blocked the flights, which could have begun this week. advocates warn of taliban persecution of those who worked with us troops. rep. salazar: hispanic vote punished deportation policy the miami republican said the hispanic vote punished the indiscriminate deportation of latino workers. un ends western sahara mission after 35 years minurso ended when the security council failed to renew it. russia vetoed a us draft backing moroccan sovereignty; a rival russian draft also failed. south africa's anc heading for worst local result with 28% counted, the anc had about 32%. full results expected sunday. who approves trials of two new ebola vaccines the outbreak, mostly in the drc, has killed more than 5,300 since may and kills about half of those infected. early results are hoped for in early 2027. ultra processed foods and children's developing brains a new study suggests ultra processed foods may affect children's brain development in ways that encourage weight gain. google to cut search for schools that reject ai student accounts lose ai tools unless administrators enable them, and schools that refuse ai entirely lose google search for students. former ftc chair lina khan called it coercion using a search monopoly. europe bets €525 million on chip design startups  supreme court november sitting under way arguments run november 2 to 10, including st. mary catholic parish v. roy (november 3) and department of labor v. sun valley orchards (november 10). desantis on the gop result the governor described the election as close to an extinction level event for republicans in many parts of the country. claim: brazil's runoff was rigged made by president trump on october 26. status: unsupported. brazil's electoral court certified the count, and the losing candidate's own party acknowledged the result. vaccines built for the new ebola strain head to trials a potential turning point in the drc's worst recorded outbreak. the midterms were rigged through fake ballots and compromised machines democrats won by importing foreigners and registering them to vote (great replacement framing) ebola is a hoax, a western bioweapon, or a scheme for aid groups to make money a scientist predicted the world ends on friday, november 13, 2026 russian deepfake campaign against democrats (matryoshka / operation overload and storm-1516) inauthentic accounts in competitive races, hitting both parties far right networks break with trump after the losses
